How to Pitch a Tent in the Rain

Rain on the first night of a trip is the worst way to learn that a tent leaks from the inside. Most of the water that ends up on your sleeping bag gets in while you are setting up, not overnight.

1. Pitch the fly first

If your tent allows it, put the rain fly up before the inner tent. Many modern tents let you clip the inner in from underneath the fly, so it never sees a drop.

2. Pick the high ground

Look for a spot that is slightly raised and away from dips where water pools. Avoid the bottom of slopes, and never camp in a dry stream bed.

3. Keep the footprint inside the floor

A groundsheet that sticks out past the tent floor catches rain and channels it underneath you. Fold the edges under so the footprint is a little smaller than the floor.
